title: Phishing emails and texts
summary: Fake messages that pretend to be your bank, a store, or a delivery company.
teach: The sender's address doesn't match the real company.
The message rushes or scares you: "act now" or "your account will be closed".
It has a link or attachment you weren't expecting.

safeMove.label: Stop
safeMove.text: don't tap links or open attachments.

safeMove.label: Spot
safeMove.text: look closely at who sent it.

safeMove.label: Block
safeMove.text: delete the message and call using a number you already trust.

title: Fake websites
summary: Look-alike websites that copy real banks and stores.
teach: Read the address from the end of the main name, just before the first slash.
Look-alike addresses swap or add letters.
Type the address yourself or use a saved bookmark.

safeMove.label: Stop
safeMove.text: don't type passwords or card numbers.

safeMove.label: Spot
safeMove.text: read the web address letter by letter from the end.

safeMove.label: Block
safeMove.text: close the tab and type the address yourself or use a saved bookmark.

title: QR code scams
summary: QR codes that lead to fake payment or sign-in pages.
teach: A QR code is just a link in disguise.
Scammers put stickers over real QR codes.
Check the address your phone shows before you open it.

safeMove.label: Stop
safeMove.text: don't scan surprise codes.

safeMove.label: Spot
safeMove.text: check if a sticker was added later, and preview the web address.

safeMove.label: Block
safeMove.text: pay through an official app, a card reader, or a trusted website.

title: Scary pop-ups
summary: Fake warnings on your screen that say your computer has a virus.
teach: Real warnings never give you a phone number to call.
A web page can't scan your computer for viruses.
Close the window or restart instead of clicking or calling.

safeMove.label: Stop
safeMove.text: don't call the phone number on the screen.

safeMove.label: Spot
safeMove.text: real security warnings never tell you to call a stranger.

safeMove.label: Block
safeMove.text: close the browser tab or restart your device.

title: Gift cards, wires and crypto
summary: Demands to pay in unusual ways that cannot be reversed.
teach: Anyone who tells you to pay with gift cards is a scammer.
Wire transfers and crypto payments cannot be cancelled or refunded.
They tell you what to say to the cashier or bank teller.

safeMove.label: Stop
safeMove.text: never buy gift cards or send a wire to resolve a problem.

safeMove.label: Spot
safeMove.text: real businesses and agencies never demand payment in gift cards or crypto.

safeMove.label: Block
safeMove.text: refuse their payment instructions and speak with someone you trust in person.

title: Family emergency calls
summary: Urgent calls claiming a grandchild or relative is hurt, arrested, or in trouble.
teach: The caller sounds panicked and begs you not to tell anyone in the family.
They demand bail money, hospital fees, or lawyer fees right away.
They may use an AI clone of your loved one's voice.

safeMove.label: Stop
safeMove.text: take a slow breath. Panic is their main weapon.

safeMove.label: Spot
safeMove.text: secrecy and extreme rush are signs of a family emergency scam.

safeMove.label: Block
safeMove.text: hang up and call your relative directly on their normal number.

title: Government and Medicare callers
summary: Callers pretending to be Social Security, Medicare, or law enforcement.
teach: They threaten arrest, frozen benefits, or legal action if you don't pay.
They ask for your Medicare number, Social Security number, or bank details.
They claim your number or card has been suspended.

safeMove.label: Stop
safeMove.text: hang up the phone. Government agencies do not call to threaten you.

safeMove.label: Spot
safeMove.text: Medicare and Social Security always contact you by official mail first.

safeMove.label: Block
safeMove.text: look up the official agency number yourself if you have concerns.

title: Messages from strangers
summary: Friendly wrong-number texts, online friends, and unsolicited investment tips.
teach: A friendly stranger texts by "mistake" and tries to start a casual conversation.
After building trust, they bring up an amazing investment or crypto opportunity.
They ask you to move your conversation to a different chat app.

safeMove.label: Stop
safeMove.text: do not reply to friendly texts from numbers you do not know.

safeMove.label: Spot
safeMove.text: anyone online offering guaranteed investment returns is trying to steal your money.

safeMove.label: Block
safeMove.text: block the sender's number and delete the conversation.

title: Prizes, charities and sweepstakes
summary: Notices claiming you won a lottery or sweepstakes you never entered.
teach: You are told you won a contest, lottery, or sweepstakes you never entered.
They insist you must pay taxes, shipping, or fees before receiving your prize.
They push you to donate immediately to an emotional or unfamiliar charity.

safeMove.label: Stop
safeMove.text: remember that you cannot win a contest or lottery you never entered.

safeMove.label: Spot
safeMove.text: if you have to pay money to collect a prize, it is a scam.

safeMove.label: Block
safeMove.text: delete the message and donate only directly to established charities you choose.

title: Shopping and delivery scams
summary: Fake online store deals, delivery problem alerts, and marketplace tricks.
teach: Popular items are advertised at impossibly low prices on unfamiliar websites.
A text says a delivery is held until you pay a small fee or update your address.
A buyer or seller insists on paying outside the official marketplace system.

safeMove.label: Stop
safeMove.text: do not click links in unexpected package delivery notices.

safeMove.label: Spot
safeMove.text: prices far below retail on unknown websites usually mean fake goods or theft.

safeMove.label: Block
safeMove.text: track your packages directly through the seller's official website.

title: Passwords and verification codes
summary: Tricks to get you to hand over one-time security codes, passwords, or PINs.
teach: A caller or message asks you to read back a six-digit code sent to your phone.
The message claims your account will be locked unless you verify your password.
They pretend to be fraud security while secretly attempting to log into your account.

safeMove.label: Stop
safeMove.text: never read or type a verification code for anyone who contacts you.

safeMove.label: Spot
safeMove.text: one-time codes are secret keys for you alone; companies never ask for them.

safeMove.label: Block
safeMove.text: hang up and change your password on the official website if worried.

title: If you think you've been scammed
summary: Clear, calm steps to take right away to protect your accounts and money.
teach: Acting in the first hour can stop bank transfers and prevent further loss.
Tell someone you trust right away; feeling embarrassed only helps the scammer.
Beware of "recovery services" that promise to get your lost money back for a fee.

safeMove.label: Stop
safeMove.text: cut off contact with the scammer immediately and take a calm breath.

safeMove.label: Spot
safeMove.text: anyone charging an upfront fee to recover stolen funds is a recovery scammer.

safeMove.label: Block
safeMove.text: call your bank's official fraud department immediately and report to the FTC.
